scope: Full existing import relevance superset plus action/hyperlink owner modules and public action enums. Every parameter-expanded unit and BDD row remains individual, linked to its exact canonical assertion contract. Merge/split are additive graph operations; generic closure preservation is not an implementation of live property, enum, collection, helper or editing APIs.
notice: upstream-license-notice.txt; test-case-map-notice.txt; public-api-map-notice.txt. Research identity pointers only; no source test bodies or assets copied.

language_security_mapping.J01: Async byte operations mergeSlides/splitSlides and camelCase operation options are separate from retained neutral snake_case model methods. Positional default mapping and typed keyword-only arguments remain per canonical API row.
language_security_mapping.J02: Each emitted archive owns its remapped relationship closure. Cross-owner model assignment remains prohibited; byte imports do not instantiate or complete live returned model handles.
language_security_mapping.J03: Operation slide selections are one-based, ordered, unique finite safe integers. Model collections remain zero-based or keyed, with exact per-collection negative, slice and inherited protocol rules.
language_security_mapping.J04: All documented action symbols and enum aliases remain separately accounted public obligations. Inert action preservation does not implement enum constructors/converters or action property accessors.
language_security_mapping.J05: Input geometry remains exact integer EMUs without implicit rescaling. Null/undefined remain distinct; no falsy coercion substitutes for selection or budget validation.
language_security_mapping.J06: Inputs are admitted bytes/streams or capability-scoped VFS inputs; output authority is supplied separately. Combined limits cover all decks and generated outputs. No ambient host file access, network, native runtime or automatic asset discovery.
language_security_mapping.J07: Navigation and external relationships remain metadata, never executed or fetched. Merge retains destination properties; split retains presentation root attributes, slide/notes dimensions, text/line-break defaults and selected dependency closure, not unrelated package properties/globals. Neither discovers identity/time/fonts; unsupported transformations reject.
language_security_mapping.J08: Operation errors use stable OfficeError codes and common CLI statuses: usage 2, content/unsupported 1, I/O 3, resource limit 4, cancelled 130. A partial publication failure lists only completed writes; this does not claim all proposed model error subclasses implemented.
language_security_mapping.J09: Closure traversal uses bounded admitted package views and owner-aware remapping. No unrestricted XPath, package callbacks, host objects or arbitrary evaluation.
language_security_mapping.J10: Shared slides.merge/slides.split operation IDs and actual schema/capabilities describe exposed behavior. No generic object evaluator or blanket alias layer. Inherited/underscore-prefixed APIs remain public obligations, including those with no upstream tests.

current_boundary: Split reconstructs a minimal independent presentation using the selected import closure. Source core properties, handout resources, show/view configuration and section/custom-show membership are not copied.

review_findings.finding: Aggregate decompression/XML checks performed only after a full per-input parse can admit work beyond the remaining combined allowance.
